missions.title: Welcome
missions.overview:
# Welcome to {app}!

> *Code a real CodeX, or its twin in the simulator.*

## We're glad you're here!

- Learn to code by completing **missions**, one short **objective** at a time.
- Code in **blocks** or in **Python**, and switch between them whenever you like: it is the same program either way.
- Run your program on a **CodeX** plugged into your computer, or on the **simulated** CodeX right here in your browser.

Press **Start** to take the tour.
missions.complete:

You've completed your first ***Mission.***

You can always click **‹ Missions** at the top of the mission pane to go back to previous Missions.

### You've learned the basics of *Missions* and *Objectives.*

missions.title: Introducing CodeX
missions.brief: Introduction to CodeX where you get your device connected and run some code!
missions.overview:
![Your guide: a friendly cartoon robot with yellow pixel eyes and a rocket flame beneath it.](bot.min.8f0189f4-svg.png)

## Greetings!

You are at the beginning of an exciting journey. I'll be your guide as you explore the immense world of *Python* with your **CodeX**.

#### Why learn coding?
* Hey, it's not just for robots anymore!
* Or laptops, mobile phones, and games,...
* Computer *chips* are making lots of things we use every day **smarter**

#### But... *Everything* computers do has to be **coded** by humans like **YOU**

As you complete this *project-based* course, you'll be learning skills that can be used to program *ANY* computer!
missions.complete:
![A happy dog with its eyes closed, leaning out a car window in the wind on a sunny country road.](CruiseDog.jpg)

### You've completed the first project!

...and you're at the start of a fantastic **adventure**. From this small first project, your journey will take you to greater
heights - more projects are ahead to *challenge* and *amaze* you!

A world of possibilities awaits you...

missions.title: Light Show
missions.brief: This project introduces the CodeX pixel LEDs, variables, and the sleep function.
missions.overview:
## This project explores the CodeX *pixel* LEDs

![A white light beam enters a glass prism and comes out split into a rainbow of colors.](Prism.jpg)

*Have you ever heard of RGB LEDs?* 
* If not you are in for a real treat!!

The CodeX has a great display, but it also has 10 individual LEDs for you to program!

### Four of the LEDs are *Smart **RGB** LEDs* aka **Pixel LEDs**

Pixel LEDs are powerful Red, Green, Blue (RGB) lights that can be a lot of fun.

Inside each pixel is a set of 3 discrete **LED** components:
* Red
* Green
* Blue

*With just 3 colors you can make the whole spectrum!!!*

### Project Goals:
* Show a sequence of colors on the Codex pixels
* Vary the speed of color Change
missions.complete:
![A pedestrian crossing signal showing a red standing figure and a red countdown reading 40.](TrafficLight.png)

## You can set the pixels to any color you want!

There are so many ways to create fun lighting schemes.

### Lights like these are used in so many applications in the real world
* Traffic lights
* Stadium scoreboards
* Concert special effects
* Smart home lighting

flow.title: Light Show
flow.promise: Light CodeX's pixels one color at a time, slow them down, and build a flashing warning sign.

chapters.title: Find the pixels
chapters.code: from codex import *

steps.say: CodeX has four **pixels**, numbered from 0. This is pixel **0**. Click it.
steps.cheer: You found pixel `0`. Now let's light it up!

steps.say: Open **Lights** and drag **set neopixel** into your program.
hints: It's the first pink block. Drop it under **when program starts**.

steps.say: Change its color to **red**.
hints: Click the arrow next to **pink**.

steps.say: Run it.
steps.cheer: STOP: the red light is on! Oh, wait, no... keep going!

chapters.title: Two in a row?
chapters.code:
from codex import *

pixels.set(0, RED)

steps.say: Drag another **set neopixel** under the first.
Make the new one **green**.
Run it. Watch closely for the red!
steps.cheer: What happened? I didn't see the red!

answers.a: It came on, but green replaced it too fast to see

steps.cheer: That's the theory. CodeX is fast: red came and went far too quickly to see. Let's slow it down.

chapters.title: Slow it down
chapters.code:
from codex import *

pixels.set(0, RED)
pixels.set(0, GREEN)

steps.say: A **wait** block makes CodeX pause. Open **Basics** and drag **wait** between red and green.
hints: Drop it just under the red block; green moves down to make room.
steps.cheer: A pause, right where you need it.

steps.say: Make it wait **1** second: click **1.5** and type **1**.
Run it.
steps.cheer: You slowed it down! Red, wait, green.

chapters.title: Name that number
chapters.code:
from codex import *
import time

pixels.set(0, RED)
time.sleep(1)
pixels.set(0, GREEN)
time.sleep(1)
pixels.set(0, BLUE)

steps.say: A **variable** is a name for a value. Open **Variables**, press **Create variable**, and name it **delay**.
Drag **set delay to** to the very top of your program, and plug a **0** from **Math** into it.
hints: Put **set delay to** above the first pink block.
Drop the **0** block from **Math** into the slot at the end of **set delay to**.

steps.say: Change that **0** to **1**.
Now drag a **delay** block onto each wait's **1**, so both waits use your variable.
hints: The round **delay** block is in **Variables**. Drop it over the number.
steps.cheer: Variables unlock the power of Python.

steps.say: Set **delay** to **0.3** and run it. One change, both waits faster!
steps.cheer: Change it once, it changes everywhere.

chapters.title: Warning sign
chapters.code:
from codex import *
import time

delay = 1
color = RED
pixels.set(0, color)
pixels.set(1, color)
pixels.set(2, color)
pixels.set(3, color)
time.sleep(delay)

steps.say: Here's half a warning sign: a **color** variable, and all four pixels set to it. Run it.
Finish the sign: after the **wait**, set **color** to **YELLOW**, light all four pixels again, then wait.
hints: Copy and paste save work: select a block, then Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V.
The yellow half is the red half again, with **YELLOW** in place of **RED**.

steps.say: Run your warning sign.
steps.cheer: Warning sign active! Everyone needs to slow... down...

flow.complete:
Pixels, sleep and variables: you made a light show.

Try it: set **delay** to **0.2** for a frantic sign, or add a third color.

missions.title: Display Games
missions.brief: Learn some CodeX display basics and create your first game.
missions.overview:
![Glowing neon sign of a game controller with the words LET'S PLAY.](DisplayGames2.jpg)

## This project explores the display

From car dashboards to giant stadium scoreboards, you see **LED** displays **everywhere**, and most of them are controlled by software. 

The CodeX display is small, but with *your code*, it can do a lot!

### Project Goals:
* Display and print **text message** *strings*
* Program buttons to determine whether they are pressed
* Make a timed *find a button* **game**
missions.complete:
![Abstract glowing lines curving down a dark screen from a checkered finish flag, like a racing game track.](CyberTall.jpg)

## Python is great for coding games
> *and you're just getting started!*

You'll soon discover a lot more possibilities as you learn more about the **CodeX**, and learn to build more complex software with text-based code.

### Real World Applications
Reading buttons and controlling LEDs... Not to mention making split-second timing decisions!
* Ever used a *remote control?*
* How about smart lighting applications for homes and schools?
* And of course, fast-twitch button-press games :-)

This kind of code is all around you!

## Nice work!!

flow.title: Display Games
flow.promise: Show pictures, words and lists on CodeX's screen, then make a game that checks your reflexes.

chapters.title: Back to the display
chapters.code:
from codex import *

display.show(pics.HEART)

steps.say: Pick **plane** in place of **heart**, then run it.
**show** can show words too. Drag a **show** block from **Screen** under the plane.
Change **Hi!** to **Ahoy**, and run it.

answers.a: Each **show** wipes the screen first, so Ahoy replaced it
Ahoy is hiding behind the plane

steps.cheer: Right. **show** always starts from a clean screen.

chapters.title: Printing text
chapters.code:
from codex import *

display.show(pics.PLANE)
display.show('Ahoy')

steps.say: **print** is different: each line goes under the last. Drag **print** from **Screen** under **Ahoy**.
steps.cheer: Now one to stack under it.

steps.say: Add a second **print** under the first, and give it your own words.
Run it.
steps.cheer: That was different! **print** keeps what's there and adds a line.

chapters.title: Branching
chapters.code:
from codex import *
import time

display.show('Hold Button A')
time.sleep(1)

steps.say: A game! This one asks you to hold **A**. Run it to see.
steps.cheer: Now CodeX needs to check whether you did.

steps.say: An **if** block lets CodeX choose. Open **Logic** and drag **if / else** under the **wait**.
hints: It's the second block in **Logic**: the one with **else**.

steps.say: From **Sensors**, drag **button A is pressed** into the **if** block's slot.
hints: Drop it on the right of the word **if**.
steps.cheer: Now CodeX can ask the question.

steps.say: From **Lights**, put a **set neopixel** in the **if** part, and make it **green**.
hints: Drop it into the gap just under **if**.
Then click its color and pick **green**.

steps.say: And a **red** one in the **else** part.
Run it, and press and hold **A** under the simulator before the second is up.
hints: The **A** button is under the simulator, on the right. Hold it down until the pixel lights.

steps.ask: You run it and don't touch **A**. What happens?
steps.cheer: The **else** part runs when the **if** isn't true.

chapters.title: For the win
chapters.code:
from codex import *
import time

display.show('Hold Button A')
time.sleep(1)
if buttons.is_pressed(BTN_A):
    pixels.set(0, GREEN)
else:
    pixels.set(0, RED)

steps.say: One round is a test. Add a second round: hold button **U**, scored on pixel **1**.
hints: Copy the first round: the **show**, the **wait** and the **if**. Then change **A** to **U** and **0** to **1**.
Select a block and press Ctrl+C, then Ctrl+V, to copy it.

steps.say: Play it. Can you get **all greens**?
steps.cheer: That game is so much fun. Too hard? Make the waits longer.

flow.complete:
Pictures, words, print and **if**: you made a game.

Add rounds for **L** and **R** on pixels 2 and 3, and see who gets four greens.

missions.title: Micro Musician
missions.brief: Play music and sounds with the CodeX and learn about code readability.
missions.overview:
## Musicians often use computers to help create music

![A sound wave drawn as a row of vertical bars of varying heights, like an audio track.](SoundWaves-svg.png)

* Drum Machines
* Keyboard synthesizers
* Recording and Mixing with Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) Software
* *...lots more ways - can you think of some?*

This is a short project, just to give you a taste of what the CodeX can do in the area of *electronic music.*

As with the display, your software can take **complete** control over the output of the CodeX, and in *future* projects you will do more customization!

### Project Goals:

* Play some of the CodeX's built-in sounds
* Learn about some code formatting to improve your code's **readability**

**Ready to make some noise?**
missions.complete:
### You can do MUCH more with sounds on the CodeX

In future lessons, you will explore more capabilities AND compose your **own** songs!

## Well done! Move ahead to more coding fun...

flow.title: Micro Musician
flow.promise: Find CodeX's speaker, play notes and a song, and give your music a picture.

chapters.title: Sound outputs
chapters.code: from codex import *

steps.say: Where does CodeX's sound come from? Find the **speaker** and click it.
hints: Spin CodeX over: the speaker is a round part on the back.

show.caption: The speaker turns your code into sound.

steps.say: Open **Sound** and drag the first **play note** block into your program.
hints: Drop it under **when program starts**.

steps.say: Drag a second **play note** under it, and run them both.
steps.cheer: Two notes, one after the other.

steps.say: Make it a tune: set the second note to **G4**, and run it.
hints: The second block is the lower one. Click its **C4** for the list of notes.

steps.ask: To CodeX a note is a number: how many times a second the speaker wiggles. C4 is 262 and G4 is 392. Which sounds higher?

chapters.title: Micro tunes
chapters.code:

audio.pitch(262, 0.4)
audio.pitch(392, 0.4)

steps.say: CodeX also plays whole songs. Drag **play sound file** from **Sound** under your notes.
Run it. If the simulator stays quiet for the song, a real CodeX plays it.
steps.cheer: ...but I think it needs a little more cowbell.

chapters.title: Multi-media
chapters.code:
from codex import *

audio.pitch(262, 0.4)
audio.pitch(392, 0.4)
audio.mp3('sounds/welcome')

steps.say: Give your music a picture: show the **music** picture before the first note plays.
hints: You need a **show** block and a **picture** block from **Screen**, both at the top.
Pick **music** in the picture block's list.

steps.say: Run your show.
steps.cheer: This is the start of something really cool.

flow.complete:
Notes, songs and a picture to go with them: you're a micro musician.

Try it: a third note, or another sound file in place of **sounds/welcome**, like **sounds/africa**.

missions.title: Heartbeat
missions.brief: Animate a beating heart on the display and learn about the power of loops.
missions.overview:
## In this project you'll give the CodeX a *beating heart.*

![A big red heart.](heart-svg.png)

Okay, not a *real* heart - that would be a little too messy!
> **But** using the display you can give the CodeX its own *digital* heart, and even make it speed up and slow down just like your own heart does.

### Project Goals:
* Code an animated heartbeat, pulsing on the LED display
* Learn how to make your code **LOOP** forever
  * And how to break out of it!
* Make the heartbeat speed *adjustable* using the **CodeX buttons**
  * **A** = *slower* and **B** = *faster*
missions.complete:
![A TV remote control with number keys, arrow keys and plus and minus buttons for volume and channel.](tv_remote.gif)

## Clicking buttons to make the speed **faster** and **slower**?

> **That code's EVERYWHERE!**

* Lighting Dimmers
* Game Controllers
* Microwave Ovens
* Vehicle Cruise Controls

### Your code could become an excellent **Visual Metronome** that could be used to set the tempo for a band!

> ...Imagine what else you might create!

flow.title: Heartbeat
flow.promise: Make a heart beat on CodeX's screen, forever, at a speed your buttons control.

chapters.title: One beat
chapters.code:
from codex import *

display.show(pics.HEART)

steps.say: A beat is big, then small. First, a pause: drag **wait** from **Basics** under the heart.
Now from **Screen**, drag **show** under the **wait**, and drop a **picture** block on its **Hi!**.
hints: Two drags: the **show** block first, then the **picture** block onto its green **Hi!**.

steps.say: Make the second one **small heart**.
hints: Click the arrow in the lower picture block.

steps.say: Run it.

chapters.title: Hearts forever
chapters.code:
from codex import *
import time

display.show(pics.HEART)
time.sleep(1)
display.show(pics.HEART_SMALL)
time.sleep(1)

steps.say: A heart beats more than once. From **Basics**, drag **forever** under your blocks.
Drag the top heart block into the loop. The blocks under it come along.

do.has:
while True:
    display.show(pics.HEART)
    time.sleep(...)
    display.show(pics.HEART_SMALL)
    time.sleep(...)

hints: Hold the top blue block and drop it in the gap inside **forever**.

steps.say: Run it. Watch a few beats, then press **Stop**.
steps.cheer: It's ALIVE! Your heart was beating.

steps.say: Look closer: run it again, press **Pause**, then **Step** a few times. Each step runs one block.
hints: **Pause** is beside **Stop** while it runs, and **Step** appears once it's paused.
steps.cheer: Big, wait, small, wait, and back to the top. Press **Stop** when you're done.

steps.ask: Without **Stop**, when would this loop end?
steps.cheer: Forever is a long time. Good thing you have **Stop**.

chapters.title: Variable speed
chapters.code:
from codex import *
import time

delay = 1
while True:
    display.show(pics.HEART)
    time.sleep(delay)
    display.show(pics.HEART_SMALL)
    time.sleep(delay)

steps.say: Now both waits use a variable, **delay**. Make the heart race: set **delay** to **0.5**, run it, then **Stop**.
steps.cheer: Speedy! Who knew half a wait could make your heart beat faster?

steps.say: Let **A** slow it down. From **Logic**, drag an **if** block to the bottom of the loop.
hints: Drop it inside **forever**, under the last **wait**.

steps.say: From **Sensors**, drag **button A was pressed** into the **if** block's slot.
steps.cheer: CodeX remembers a press, even mid-beat.

steps.say: From **Variables**, put **change delay by** inside the **if**, and make it **0.2**.
hints: Drop it in the gap under **if**, then click its **1** and type **0.2**.

steps.say: Run it, press **A** a few times, then **Stop**.
steps.cheer: Resting heartbeat. Your CodeX is so calm right now.

chapters.title: Variable speed heart
chapters.code:
from codex import *
import time

delay = 0.5
while True:
    display.show(pics.HEART)
    time.sleep(delay)
    display.show(pics.HEART_SMALL)
    time.sleep(delay)
    if buttons.was_pressed(BTN_A):
        delay = delay + 0.2

steps.say: Now let **B** speed it up.
hints: Copy the **if** block for **A**, and change **A** to **B**.
Speeding up means a smaller delay: change it by **-0.2**.

steps.say: Run it: speed it up with **B**, slow it down with **A**. **Stop** when you're done.
steps.cheer: You're in control of the beat.

flow.complete:
Loops, buttons and a variable that changes as it runs: you built a heart with a speed control.

Try it: what happens if you press **B** a lot? Could you stop **delay** going below zero?
